property_summary: Invariant: after a user deposits X and then calls withdrawAll, the contract's recorded credit for that user becomes zero (i.e., withdraw clears the user's credit); the mutant that does the external call before zeroing allows a reentrant attacker to drain funds and leave the user's credit non-zero, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any caller who deposits >0, after withdrawAll returns the contract's recorded credit for that caller is zero; the mutant that calls the recipient before clearing credit allows a reentrant attacker to drain funds while leaving credit non-zero, breaking this property for some inputs.

For any depositor who deposited a positive amount, after calling withdrawAll the depositor's recorded credit is always zero in the correct contract; the mutant that performs the external call before zeroing allows a reentrant attacker to cause a nonzero recorded credit (or inconsistent balance) and thus violates this rule for some inputs.

For any depositor and deposit amount > 0, after calling withdrawAll the contract's address(c).balance decreases by exactly the withdrawn amount (i.e., funds are transferred out only once); the mutant that does the external call before zeroing the creditor allows a reentrant attacker to cause extra withdrawals and thus makes address(c).balance decrease by more than the original withdrawal for some inputs.

For any depositor who deposited a positive amount and then calls withdrawAll, after the call completes the contract's recorded credit for that depositor is zero; the mutant that performs the external call before zeroing allows a reentrant attacker to reenter and leave the recorded credit non-zero, violating the rule for some inputs.

After a successful withdrawAll call by any actor with nonzero credit, the contract's credit[actor] becomes zero (reference preserves this invariant for all inputs); the mutant that omits zeroing allows credit[actor] to remain > 0 after withdrawAll for some inputs.

For any caller and any deposit amount, after calling withdrawAll the caller's recorded credit is zero in the reference implementation; the mutant that omits zeroing can leave the caller's credit > 0 after withdrawal (e.g., when the external call to the caller succeeds), so the property is violated for some inputs.

For every caller and deposit amount, after depositing and then calling withdrawAll, the reference contract always sets the caller's credit to zero (so address(c).balance decreases by that amount and subsequent withdrawAll does nothing); the mutant that omits zeroing can leave the caller's credit nonzero after a successful external call, so address(c).balance behavior (and the persisted credit) differs for some inputs.

For any depositor and deposit amount, if the depositor's external fallback reverts when receiving funds, then withdrawAll must revert (reference always reverts because it zeros credit before the external call and still performs the call which reverts, preserving credit as before; the mutant that omits zeroing will still revert the external call but leaves credit non-zero which changes post-state behavior — asserting that a failed withdrawAll call does NOT change the depositor's recorded credit distinguishes them).

For every caller and deposit amount, after a successful withdrawAll call the caller's recorded credit is reset to zero by the reference implementation; the mutant that omits zeroing can leave the caller's credit > 0 for some inputs (when the external call succeeds), so the property (credit becomes zero) is violated by the mutant.

For any caller and any positive deposit amount, calling withdrawAll on the correct contract decreases the contract's on-chain balance by exactly the withdrawn amount (and does not increase it); the mutant that adds to balance instead can increase the contract balance after a withdrawal, violating this invariant for some inputs.

For any depositor and deposit amount, calling withdrawAll always succeeds (does not return false / revert) for the correct contract because low-level call forwards all gas and will propagate any revert into require(callResult) succeeding only when the external transfer succeeds; replacing call with send can fail (returns false) when the recipient's fallback uses more than stipend or otherwise causes send to fail, so the mutant can cause withdrawAll to revert/fail for some depositor and amount — the reference never leaves the contract with a failed transfer under the same external adversary behavior.

For any depositor and deposit amount, if a recipient's fallback uses more than the 2300 gas stipend (causing send to fail) then the reference C's withdrawAll still succeeds (low-level call forwards gas so transfer succeeds) while the mutant using send will cause withdrawAll to revert — therefore withdrawAll should never revert for the reference when interacting with a contract fallback that reverts on limited gas, but the mutant will revert for some deposit amounts and actors.

For any depositor and any recipient contract whose fallback deliberately uses more than the 2300 gas stipend, the reference C's withdrawAll will succeed (not revert) and transfer the deposited funds out, whereas the mutant that uses send can fail (revert) for some such recipient and amount.
